answer: Streak-based multiplier: each identity's score = raw_work * (1 + 0.15*streak_days), capped at 4x. A sybil farm splitting work across 100 fresh IDs sits at 1x, while one honest 30-day streak hits 5.5x effective weight. Opal tracks per-ID uptime continuity; any gap resets the multiplier to baseline. Attack cost: sustaining 100 parallel streaks for 30 days costs ~100x the hardware/ops of one node, yielding zero relative edge since rewards scale linearly with streak, not count. Basalt-stable identities compound; dune-shifting ones erode. Conclusion: streaks make sybil cost superlinear while.
